newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-LOLA RETURNING TO FORMULA ONE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LOLA RETURNING TO FORMULA ONE.

text.p: British-based racing car maker Lola confirmed on Tuesday it is returning to Formula One next season for the first time since 1993.
But they have left it late to renew their challenge for Grand Prix honours -- the new car will not be unveiled until February, less than a month before the 1997 season starts in Australia.

Lola spokeswoman Anne Hale said: "The directors are confident that they can deliver the new car within the time-scale. Some of the engineers are already employed in Formula One...but time is of the essence."
The news ends months of speculation about whether the team, which has won the Indy Car championship five times, would return to top-level motor racing outside the United States.
Lola confirmed their decision after an announcement by credit card company Mastercard that they would be backing the new team with a four-year sponsorship deal.

Brett Trafford, marketing director for the Lola Formula One team said: "We have always thought seriously about Formula One -- it offers stability for the company in that it is likely to remain on the calender for many years. We think that it is good for Lola because the technical developments produced in Formula One will filter down to other aspects of our motor sport operation."
He said the budget for the new team was likely to be in the region of 30 million pounds sterling ($48 million) although he declined to reveal how much of that would be covered by the Mastercard deal.

Trafford added that backing from outside the tobacco industry, which invests heavily in Formula One, was important given the threat of legislation which could cut back on the amount of tobacco advertising at sporting events.
The team said they hoped to name a driver "within the next two weeks" and Trafford confirmed that Lola had been speaking to the Dane, Tom Kristensen, a leading Formula 3000 driver.
Brazilian Ricardo Rosset, dropped by TWR-Arrows, and his compatriot Ricardo Zonta, a double winner in this year's Formula 3000 series, have also been linked with the team.

"Realistically it is going to be very hard. It is a privilege just to be in Formula One; everyone competing in it at the moment is very good so we realise it is going to be difficult," added Trafford.

Lola confirmed last month they had embarked on a five-year project to build a new engine for Formula One in a project costing up to 10 million pounds ($16.5 million). They last contested the 1993 campaign with the BMS Lola Ferrari.

The company -- founded in 1958 by current chairman and managing director Eric Broadley -- has a long and illustrious association with top-level motor sport. Although it has only one Formula One victory to its name, the Italian Grand Prix in 1967, it has a history of success in Indy cars, Formula 3000 in Europe and Japan and the Le Mans 24 hours.
The attractions for both team and sponsor are obvious. Formula One is now recognised as one of the the most-watched sports in the world with a global TV audience of 45 billion in 200 countries.
Lola will join Jackie Stewart's new works Ford team as the new boys on the grid next year, bringing the probable number of teams up to 12 for the 1997 season.
